sections.title: The letter ti
paragraphs: The letter is called (ti) /ti/. It makes the sound in (tempo) /ˈtɛm.po/, which means time, weather. This letter always makes only one sound.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper front teeth. Block the air completely for a brief moment. Drop your tongue away quickly so the breath bursts out cleanly. A plosive is a consonant where the air stops for a moment and then bursts out. Put your fingers on your throat to check. Your voice stays off.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in all positions. You hear it at the start of words like (tempo) /ˈtɛm.po/. When you see it written twice, hold the sound longer, as in (notte) /ˈnɔt.te/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not blow a puff of air when you release this sound. Touch your upper teeth directly, not the ridge behind them. English tea starts further back and sends out a little puff of air. Keep the sound dry, crisp and clear.
